html: The Accomac were an Algonquian-speaking people of the Eastern Shore of Virginia, on the peninsula between Chesapeake Bay and the Atlantic. In 1607 they paid tribute to the Powhatan paramount chiefdom across the bay, but under their own chief, Debedeavon, whom the English called the "Laughing King", they made friends with the colonists of Jamestown and granted them land. English settlement spread on the Eastern Shore from the 1620s and the Accomac lost their land; by the 1700s they had largely merged with neighbours such as the Occohannock. Accomack County, Virginia, keeps their name. To the north lived the Nanticoke.
